key_insight: A local open-weight OCR+LLM pipeline on a single consumer GPU can accurately turn faxed oncology referral packets into structured clinical data.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual chart-reading burden for referral intake while keeping protected health information on-device.
method: Generated 200 synthetic colorectal cancer referral packets from simulated records and rendered them as image-only faxes.
Used OvisOCR2 for transcription and Qwen3.8-27B for structured information extraction.
Compared 20 clinical outcomes against ground truth on 140 validation packets.
evidence_signal: Across 11,993 extracted facts, the pipeline showed 0.990 weighted accuracy, with laboratory values at 98.9%, dates at 99.7%, diagnoses at 100%, and no fabricated facts.
watch_item: Results were based on synthetic referral packets, so real-world performance on messy, diverse faxed records still needs validation.
paper_title: Extraction of clinical information from faxed medical records using a small local large language model pipeline on consumer hardware
